note: Delaware has an Institutional Abuse Unit inside the Department of Services for Children, Youth and Their Families that investigates abuse or neglect of a child while at a facility or program, so an institutional report does not get handled as an ordinary family case. Delaware also places a duty on every licensed practitioner to report another practitioner they reasonably believe is doing something that would be grounds for discipline - useful if you are a clinician who has seen something and is wondering whether you may say so.

civil_injury.summary: Two years from the date the injury happened, for any personal-injury claim, including assault, battery and negligence.
civil_injury.quote: No action for the recovery of damages upon a claim for alleged personal injuries shall be brought after the expiration of 2 years from the date upon which it is claimed that such alleged injuries were sustained
civil_injury.note: False imprisonment has no separate section in chapter 81; if it is not treated as a personal-injury claim it may fall under the three-year general period in § 8106 (not re-read; not verified).

civil_minor_tolling.summary: Delaware's childhood tolling rule (three years after the disability ends) only covers the claims listed in sections 8101-8115, and the two-year personal-injury deadline is section 8119, outside that range. So for physical-injury claims the clock likely runs from the injury even if the victim was a child. Only sexual-abuse claims get special treatment.
civil_minor_tolling.quote: If a person entitled to any action comprehended within §§ 8101-8115 of this title, shall have been ... under disability of infancy ..., this chapter shall not be a bar to such action during the continuance of such disability, nor until the expiration of 3 years from the removal thereof.
civil_minor_tolling.note: The reading that § 8116 does not reach § 8119 comes from the text's own section range; Delaware case law on this point was not verified. Claims that fall within §§ 8101-8115 (e.g. the three-year § 8106 period, if it applies) would be tolled until three years after 18. Sexual abuse of a minor has no civil limit (§ 8145, out of scope). No general discovery rule for non-sexual abuse was found in the statute.

civil_government_claims.summary: The State and its employees are immune for good-faith discretionary acts done without gross or wanton negligence. Counties, towns and other local bodies are immune from tort suits except narrow negligence exceptions (vehicles, public buildings, pollution); a local ordinance may require notice but cannot bar a suit if notice is given within one year.
civil_government_claims.quote: Any political subdivision may enact a notice requirement by ordinance, so long as said notice requirement does not bar suit if notice is given within 1 year of occurrence.
civil_government_claims.note: § 4011(a): 'all governmental entities and their employees shall be immune from suit on any and all tort claims seeking recovery of damages' except as provided. § 4001 (https://delcode.delaware.gov/title10/c040/sc01/index.html) makes the plaintiff prove the absence of an immunity element, e.g. gross or wanton negligence or bad faith. No statewide notice-of-claim deadline was found; the normal § 8119 deadline applies to any suit that is allowed.

criminal_child_abuse.summary: Child abuse causing permanent injury (first degree) is a class A felony and can be charged at any time. Other felony child abuse (second and third degree, child torture, felony endangering) must be charged within five years; misdemeanor child abuse within three years. The clock is not paused until the victim turns 18.
criminal_child_abuse.quote: (a) A prosecution for murder or any class A felony ... may be commenced at any time. (b) ... (1) A prosecution for any felony except murder or any class A felony ... must be commenced within 5 years after it is committed;
criminal_child_abuse.note: § 1103C, added by 84 Del. Laws c. 126 (2023): child abuse in the first degree, 'serious physical injury to a child and that injury causes permanent disfigurement, permanent impairment of health, or permanent loss or impairment of a bodily organ', is a class A felony, so no limit. § 1103B (serious physical injury) is class B, § 1103A class D, § 1103 class A misdemeanor; text read at https://delcode.delaware.gov/title11/c005/sc05/index.html. The no-limit rule in § 205(e) covers sexual offenses and trafficking of minors only. The clock stops while the accused is fleeing or hiding (§ 205(h)).

criminal_felony_assault.summary: Felony assault (first or second degree) must be charged within five years; no limit if it is a class A felony. Misdemeanor assault (class A misdemeanor): three years; lesser misdemeanors: two years.
criminal_felony_assault.quote: (1) A prosecution for any felony except murder or any class A felony, or any attempt to commit said crimes, must be commenced within 5 years after it is committed; (2) A prosecution for a class A misdemeanor must be commenced within 3 years after it is committed;

channels.name: Delaware Division of Professional Regulation
channels.what_it_can_do: Houses the Board of Mental Health and Chemical Dependency Professionals, the Board of Professional Counselors and the psychology board. The boards monitor complaints against their licensees, hold formal hearings and impose sanctions.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed mental health or chemical dependency professional in Delaware.
channels.how: Submit the complaint in writing to the Director of the Division of Professional Regulation. At the Board's next scheduled meeting a contact person is appointed and given a copy of it.
channels.note: Under Title 24 Chapter 30, every licensee has a duty to report in writing where they reasonably believe another practitioner or health care provider has engaged in conduct that would be grounds for discipline.

channels.name: Delaware Child Abuse Report Line (Institutional Abuse Unit)
channels.what_it_can_do: The statutory 24-hour report line. Where the complaint concerns abuse or neglect of a child while at a facility or program, the Department's Institutional Abuse Unit or law enforcement investigates it.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Delaware program.
channels.how: Call the report line at any hour.
channels.phone_note: 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

channels.name: Delaware Office of Child Care Licensing (OCCL)
channels.what_it_can_do: Investigates complaints that a licensed facility has broken the licensing rules, including the regulations governing residential child care facilities.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It has no authority over financial matters and does not investigate personal disputes. Abuse and neglect go to the Child Abuse Report Line instead.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed Delaware residential child care facility, where the issue is a licensing breach.
channels.how: File a confidential complaint online, or call the office for the county the facility is in.
channels.phone_note: Kent and Sussex counties; also 302-739-5487. New Castle County 302-892-5800.

channels.name: Disability Rights Delaware (Community Legal Aid Society)
channels.what_it_can_do: Delaware's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Delaware program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
channels.note: Operates as part of the Community Legal Aid Society; its site is declasi.org.
